statement: At abundant food, feeding rate is at a maximum, independent of food density.

scores.rationale: Multiple snippets directly corroborate the stylized fact. Snippet [8] explicitly states the fact verbatim, and snippets [2], [5], [10], [12], and [14] describe the hyperbolic (type II) functional response in which ingestion/feeding rate saturates to a maximum at high food density and becomes effectively independent of food concentration (e.g., the incipient limiting level in [2], the >80% saturation threshold in [12]). Snippets [3], [7], [9], [13] support the related scaled functional response framework where f approaches 1 at abundant food. The only contradicting note is [18], which discusses social/ratio-dependent feeding effects making feeding rate not solely a function of food density, but this is presented as an open extension rather than a refutation of the saturation principle. Overall the corpus strongly and consistently supports the fact.

scores.rationale: None of the 18 snippets directly addresses the functional-response claim that feeding rate saturates to a maximum independent of food density at abundant food. The corpus is dominated by population ecology, density-dependence, foraging behavior, and reproduction topics. A few snippets touch tangentially on relative food availability (snippet 1, theoretical maximum consumption rate) or saturation/satiation effects (snippets 10/15, animals being more selective when food is common), but none provides explicit evidence affirming or refuting a saturating maximum feeding rate. Snippet 1's reference to a 'theoretical maximum consumption rate' is the closest conceptual link but does not test the independence-from-density claim. Therefore evidence is weak/sparse with no clear support or contradiction, leaving the corpus essentially uninformative on this stylized fact.
